 Virginia voter checklist: What to know before casting your ballot
 Election day now just two weeks away!
 Bella Walser , Community Journalist
 Published:  October 20, 2026 at 8:16 AM Tags:  Decision 2026 , Voting , Elections , Roanoke , Virginia (Tommy Martino, Copyright 2024 The Associated Press. All rights reserved) Virginia voters head to the polls Nov. 3 with a packed ballot — and the state’s top election official has a simple but critical reminder before anyone steps into a voting booth.
 “So one thing, don’t forget to turn your ballot over and check the other side because we don’t want anybody missing races and ballot questions on the other side,” said Steve Koski, Virginia Commissioner of Elections.
 Recommended Videos
 Every Virginia voter will weigh in on the same U.S. Senate race and three proposed constitutional amendments . Depending on the congressional district, voters will also decide a U.S. House race and may decide on local contests .
 Your Election Day checklist
 Before heading to the polls, Koski recommends working through a short checklist to avoid some of the most common voter mistakes.
 Preview your sample ballot. Every voter will see the same U.S. Senate race featuring Democratic incumbent Mark Warner against Republican challenger Bert Mizusawa 
 Every voter will decide three constitutional amendments covering reproductive rights, marriage equality and restoration of voting rights. 
 U.S. House races and local contests will vary by address. 
 Check your registration. Voters can register online at vote.elections.virginia.gov until Friday, Oct. 23. Those who miss that deadline can still register in person and cast a provisional ballot all the way through Election Day, Nov. 3. 
 Confirm your polling location. This is one of the most common mistakes voters make, according to Koski — and it can cost someone their vote. “You have to go to the correct polling location where you’re registered or if you’re doing same-day registration, the polling location for your residential address. So it’s really important to verify that information,” Koski said. 
 Voters should not assume their polling place is the same as in previous years. Locations can change, and a voter cannot cast a regular ballot at the wrong precinct. 
 Know what ID to bring. Virginia accepts several forms of identification, including a driver’s license and military ID. Voters without an accepted ID still have options available to them. 
 Key dates to know
 Friday, Oct. 23: Online voter registration deadline; deadline to request an absentee ballot 
 Saturday, Oct. 31: Early voting ends 
 Tuesday, Nov. 3: Election Day 
 Voters can find their polling location, check registration status and preview their sample ballot at vote.elections.virginia.gov.
